clue.text: Name article found in English mine

indicators.note: found in says the article sits inside the word for mine

parts.note: a pit is a mine, as in a coal pit
'the' is the definite article

explanation.surface: A name and an article are discovered in an English mine, like a report of a mining find.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive byname or label given to someone, so it can stand for a name.

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the heart of sweet is its middle letter E, and the 's adds S
livid can mean ashen or pale

explanation.surface: A lover is furious about being passed over.
explanation.walkthrough: ES + PALE gives ESPALE, read backwards under 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or elapse, so the verbs are synonyms for time going by.

clue.text: Serve up in pub restaurant, commonly

indicators.note: in means the reversed word sits inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, i.e. reversed

parts.note: to serve someone is to aid them

explanation.surface: A pub with a restaurant serving food upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, going for an Indian means eating at an Indian restaurant, hence 'commonly' marks the colloquial use.

clue.text: The French confused about love hereafter

indicators.note: about means the muddled letters go round the letter for love
confused means muddled up, so the letters of the French are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: The French are bewildered about love in the afterlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforth means from now on, the same as hereafter used as an adverb about future time.

clue.text: Possibly watch bank hiding money's source

indicators.note: hiding means the bank word conceals the single letter inside it

parts.note: a tier is a row or bank, as of seats

indicators.note: source means origin, so take the first letter of money

explanation.surface: Perhaps a security watch on a bank hiding the source of its money.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is one kind of timepiece, and a timer is any device measuring time, so 'possibly' marks an example.

indicators.note: beginning to points at just the opening letter of the next word, plane

parts.note: lumber is sawn timber, i.e. wood

explanation.surface: A craftsman starts work by planing a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber is a skilled tradesman who fits pipes, so artisan works as a loose synonym for a manual craftsman.

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of male cop in are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man of the law carrying out a raid, or bust.
explanation.walkthrough: Bust is both the anagram signal and a police raid, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A policeman is a male officer of the police force, which is exactly a male cop.

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the four preceding words

explanation.surface: A description of an impulsive feeling that usually comes on rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a sudden strong impulse or desire, typically arising on a whim without thought.

parts.note: to beat is to hit
providing means if, as a condition

indicators.note: endless means drop the final letter of the word for chill

parts.note: ice is a chill, as in to ice a drink

explanation.surface: A sublime hit song, as long as it never stops being cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatific means blissful or radiantly happy, the look of heavenly joy, a sense close to sublime.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: going to bed for the night

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a bashful lover; the question mark flags that the second sense is a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Retiring is an adjective meaning shy, and the verb form means withdrawing to sleep.

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so take every other letter of vague

parts.note: a den is a small private room or study

explanation.surface: A poet described as doing vague, intermittent study.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet of the twentieth century, so the answer is an example of a poet.

indicators.note: embraces means the married worker pair wraps around the word for ally

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker
to ally oneself is to align oneself with someone

explanation.surface: A spiteful married labourer hugs a friend, a picture of a two-faced colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: Malignant means malicious or intending harm, so it fits hurtful in the sense of wishing injury.

clue.text: Son beat rivalry boxing, say, rascal

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

indicators.note: boxing means the beat and rivalry words enclose the abbreviation for say

parts.note: to cap is to outdo or beat
a race is a contest of rivalry, as in the arms race
say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A son beats a rival in a boxing match, and someone calls him a rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegrace is an old word for a mischievous scoundrel, a synonym for rascal.

clue.text: Purveyor of pork pies in EastEnders?

definitions.text: Purveyor of pork pies in EastEnders?

parts.words: Purveyor of pork pies in EastEnders
parts.note: pork pies is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, and EastEnders are Cockneys, so someone selling pork pies there tells untruths

explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is both a BBC soap set in London's East End and a name for Cockneys, whose rhyming slang turns pork pies into lies; the clue pretends to be about a butcher in the soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A liar dispenses falsehoods, and in rhyming slang those falsehoods are pork pies.

clue.text: Mother's single eating beef and cheese

indicators.note: eating means the mother and single words take in the word for beef

parts.note: ma is mother, with the 's adding S
single means one
to beef and to carp both mean to complain

explanation.surface: A mother's single dish of beef with cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef is a verb here, complaining, not meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascarpone is a soft, creamy Italian cheese used in tiramisu.

clue.text: Sentence of criminal nominated for discharge

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

indicators.note: discharge suggests firing off or releasing, so the letters of nominated are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal is sentenced, though nominated for early release from prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A condemnation is a judicial sentence pronouncing someone guilty and fixing their punishment.

clue.text: Degree of party talk holding court

indicators.note: holding means the party and talk words grip the court abbreviation

parts.note: a do is a party
to orate is to talk, especially pompously

explanation.surface: A graduation party where someone talks, holding court.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is the highest university degree, such as a PhD.

clue.text: Gleaming gents finally with no bowl?

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of gents

parts.note: a pot is a bowl-shaped vessel
less as a suffix means without, as in pot-less

explanation.surface: The gents' toilets end up gleaming, though the toilet bowl is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means perfectly clean, so it fits gleaming as a description of a scrubbed surface.

indicators.note: circumventing means going round, so the beast word encloses the trap word

parts.note: a brute is a beast
a net is a trap for catching animals

explanation.surface: A dark-haired animal escaping a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with dark brown hair, used here adjectivally.

indicators.note: cracking means breaking apart, so the letters of hones cryptic are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone sharpens their skill at cracking cryptic crosswords and shows real brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyrotechnics, besides fireworks, means a dazzling display of skill or virtuosity, i.e. brilliance.

parts.note: tins are containers

indicators.note: exterior means the outside letters, first and last, of enamel

explanation.surface: Showy containers with an enamelled outside finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel used as an adjective means showy but cheap, which is what gaudy describes.

clue.text: US soldiers catching deserter getting free

indicators.note: catching means the soldiers surround the deserter word

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is someone who deserts, as rats desert a sinking ship

explanation.surface: American troops catch a deserter, who is then set free.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means without charge, so it means free in the costless sense.

indicators.note: reportedly signals the word for stacks is said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: stacks means loads or tons, as in stacks of money

explanation.surface: A cellar described as having barrels piled in stacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask for wine or beer, so the plural means big barrels.

clue.text: Officer regarding one dismal troop retreating

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole string of words is read in reverse

parts.note: re means regarding, as in a letter heading
I is the Roman numeral for one
drab means dull or dismal
a mob is a crowd or troop

explanation.surface: A report on an officer leading a sorry troop into retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + I + DRAB + MOB gives REIDRABMOB, which read backwards is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardier is a non-commissioned officer in the Royal Artillery, ranking like a corporal.

clue.text: Hit bushes, perhaps catching large grouse

indicators.note: catching means the beat word takes in the letter for large

parts.note: beaters hit the bushes to drive game birds out on a shoot, so this is to beat

explanation.surface: Beaters strike the bushes on a shoot and flush a big grouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Grouse looks like the game bird, but it is the verb to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleat is to whine or complain feebly, a synonym of the verb grouse.

indicators.note: covering means the record word wraps around the letter for queen

parts.note: to cut a record is to record it
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A brief recording made of the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt means brusquely brief in speech, so short in the rude sense.

clue.text: In movement, our agenda includes train

indicators.note: includes means the answer lies inside the run of words movement our agenda

explanation.surface: A political movement claims its agenda covers training.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a retinue of attendants following an important person, which is what an entourage is.

parts.note: an actor performing is on, as in on stage
the set is where a film is shot, so being in a film puts you on set

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an actor's start was in a film.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means the beginning of something, especially something unpleasant, as in the onset of winter.

indicators.note: purchasing means taking hold of, so the words circumspect regarding grip the answer

explanation.surface: Advice to be careful when buying alcoholic spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is a ghost or apparition, so it is a spirit in the supernatural sense.

parts.note: bloomers here are flowering plants, not knickers, and a garden framework supports climbing ones

explanation.walkthrough: Bloomers suggests old-fashioned knickers held up by elastic or braces; here they are plants that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice of wood or wire used to support climbing plants such as roses.
